stem: Meena starts facing West. She turns right, then turns right again, then turns left. Which direction does she now face?

per_option_rationale.rationale: West -> right(CW) = North -> right(CW) = East -> left(ACW) = North.
East is the result after two right turns only; the final left turn was not applied.
South results from treating all three turns as right turns (West->N->E->S), ignoring that the last turn is a left.
West is the starting direction; a right followed by a left cancel, but a second right in between shifts the net result.

explanation: Track heading after each turn: West + right(CW) = North; North + right(CW) = East; East + left(ACW) = North. Final direction is North.

explanation_sections.punchline: Right-right-left from West: N, then E, then back to N - the last left undoes only one of the two rights.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: apply turns one at a time using clockwise order N->E->S->W. Right = +1 step, Left = -1 step. Start West(3): +1=N(0), +1=E(1), -1=N(0). Final: North.
explanation_sections.lesson: Count each turn separately using a direction index; do not try to combine or cancel turns mentally without tracking intermediate headings.
explanation_sections.timing: 40-50 seconds. The main trap is stopping after two right turns (gives East, option 2). Another trap is treating left as another right (gives South, option 3).
